newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close slightly firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close slightly firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed slightly firmer in quiet trade on Monday, with the market awaiting the reaction of U.S. Treasuries to the results of Tuesday's U.S. elections, analysts said.
"The market was very quiet today. I think most people are waiting to see what's going to happen in the U.S.," said Joe Lee, a Toronto-based portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.25 to C$112.45 to yield 6.964 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark rose 7/32 to yield 6.66 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 30 basis points from 31 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
"It's been very quiet all day. Domestic clients have been waiting for the election," said one Toronto-based trader. "Today has been very stable after the opening."

Canadian dealers said there is concern that if Democrats regain control of Congress in tomorrow's elections, U.S. Treasuries could weaken. Analysts said weakness in the world's largest fixed income market could then easily spillover into Canada.
Canadian building permits and labour income data released this morning had little impact on bond prices, analysts said.
The very short end of the Canadian yield curve was stronger today, buoyed by speculation the Bank of Canada will soon cut short-term interest rates, dealers said.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 rose C$0.15 to C$105.00 to yield 6.320 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark rose 6/32 to yield 6.35 percent.
The spread between the bonds shrank to three basis points from four basis points on Friday. The three-month cash bill traded at 2.95 percent against the U.S. bill at 5.14 percent.
